fatal_errors: The proposed AlCrTiZrMo film and induced ZrTiO4 layer are not the target as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy with an L12/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The matched DS2205 comparator is replaced by an untreated specimen of the same HEA, so the principal controlled comparison is not reconstructed.
The proposed 3.5 wt.% NaCl environment conflicts with the target tribocorrosion tests in deionized water over 25–100 °C.

The thermal shock is incorrectly treated as a means of deliberately preforming a protective surface oxide rather than as three rapid 1100 °C heating/quenching cycles used to compare bulk phase stability.
The prediction omits the central nonmonotonic temperature response, with minimum degradation near 50 °C and increased film disruption at 100 °C.

It predicts mainly a reduced corrosion component with similar wear, whereas the target result is dominated by substantially lower wear volume and wear rate, along with improved electrochemical behavior.
explanation: The hypothesis is scientifically plausible in a general HEA tribocorrosion context: dynamic passive-film formation and removal can govern coupled degradation, and E1 directly supports improved tribocorrosion after annealing an AlCrTiZrMo coating. However, it reconstructs a different material system, treatment purpose, electrolyte, baseline, and expected outcome. Its mechanism overlaps only at the broad level of competition between depassivation and repassivation; it misses the target's temperature-dependent transition from abrasion to polishing to disrupted oxidative or third-body wear, as well as the role of retained L12/B2 lamellae and homogeneous Cr availability. The proposed experiment could test whether a pretreatment improves performance, but it would not cleanly establish that passive-layer stability is the governing cause unless film state is independently manipulated or quantified while hardness and microstructure are controlled. E2 concerns cavitation rather than reciprocating sliding, and E3 supports compositional strengthening and separate wear/corrosion behavior more than the asserted passive-film mechanism. Thus, this is a supported alternative hypothesis rather than a reconstruction of the hidden study.
